# Ezekiel 5 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** "And you, O son of man, take a sharp sword. Use it as a barber's razor and pass it over your head and your beard. Then take scales for weighing and divide the hair.

**2** A third part you shall burn in the fire in the midst of the city, when the days of the siege are completed. And a third part you shall take and strike with the sword all around the city. And a third part you shall scatter to the wind, and I will unsheathe the sword after them.

**3** And you shall take from these a small number and bind them in the skirts of your robe.

**4** And of these again you shall take some and cast them into the midst of the fire and burn them in the fire. From there a fire will come out into all the house of Israel."

**5** Thus says the Lord GOD: "This is Jerusalem. I have set her in the center of the nations, with countries all around her.

**6** And she has rebelled against My rules by doing wickedness more than the nations, and against My statutes more than the countries all around her; for they have rejected My rules and have not walked in My statutes."

**7** Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: "Because you are more turbulent than the nations that are all around you, and have not walked in My statutes or obeyed My rules, and have not even acted according to the rules of the nations that are all around you,"

**8** therefore thus says the Lord GOD: "Behold, I, even I, am against you. And I will execute judgments in your midst in the sight of the nations.

**9** And because of all your abominations I will do with you what I have never yet done, and the like of which I will never do again.

**10** Therefore fathers shall eat their sons in your midst, and sons shall eat their fathers. And I will execute judgments on you, and any of you who survive I will scatter to all the winds.

**11** I will withdraw from you and show no pity, and I will have no compassion because of all your detestable practices, declares the Lord GOD.

**12** I will withdraw from you and show no pity, and I will have no compassion because of all your detestable practices, declares the Lord GOD.

**13** I will withdraw from you and show no pity, and I will have no compassion because of all your detestable practices, declares the Lord GOD.

**14** I will withdraw from you and show no pity, and I will have no compassion because of all your detestable practices, declares the Lord GOD.

**15** You shall be a reproach and a taunt, a warning and a horror, to the nations all around you, when I execute judgments on you in anger and fury and with furious rebukes — I am the LORD; I have spoken —

**16** when I send against you the deadly arrows of famine, arrows for destruction, which I will send to destroy you, and when I bring more and more famine upon you and break your supply of bread.

**17** I will send famine and wild beasts against you, and they will rob you of your children. Pestilence and blood shall pass through you, and I will bring the sword upon you. I am the LORD; I have spoken."

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Ezekiel 5.

- **5:2** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **5:3** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **5:6** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **5:10** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **5:16** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **5:11** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **5:1-2**: The hair-shaving sign-act: hair symbolizes life/identity. Three portions represent Jerusalem's three fates: fire (siege), sword (battle), wind (exile). The razor-as-sword blurs instrument of grooming with instrument of death.
- **5:5**: Betokh ha-goyim samtihah — 'in the midst of the nations I set her.' Jerusalem's centrality is both privilege and responsibility. Her sin is worse because of her position.
- **5:10**: Avot yokhelu vanim — 'fathers shall eat sons.' Cannibalism during siege (cf. 2 Kgs 6:28-29, Lam 4:10) — the ultimate reversal of parental care.

### LOGOS
- **5:1-4**: The three-part division of hair creates a devastatingly precise prophecy: siege fire, sword in battle, and scattering in exile account for the entire population. The few hairs saved hint at a remnant.
- **5:5-6**: Jerusalem's sin exceeds even pagan nations — a shocking claim. God's people are held to a higher standard because of greater revelation, and their failure is proportionally worse.
- **5:10**: The horror of cannibalism in siege conditions is well-documented in ancient Near Eastern siege accounts. Ezekiel uses it as the supreme symbol of covenant curses fulfilled (Deut 28:53).

### PNEUMA
- **5:1-4**: Shaving your head and beard was deeply shameful in the ancient world. Then burning, chopping, and scattering the hair — God is asking Ezekiel to act out Jerusalem's total humiliation on his own body.
- **5:5-6**: The shocking claim: Jerusalem is worse than the pagan nations around her. Not just failing to meet God's standards — failing to meet even basic human decency. Privilege without faithfulness becomes the worst kind of guilt.
- **5:10**: This verse is almost unbearable — parents eating their children during siege. It's not metaphor. It's the reality of what happens when a city is starved into madness. God doesn't sanitize the horror.

— SOPHIA
